comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC report results for an 'All Other' category within their financial disclosures for 2024, but they report opposite directions in net income/loss. C reported a net loss of $2.4 billion, which increased from the prior year, driven by lower revenues and lower income tax benefits. In contrast, BAC reported a net loss in All Other of $1.6 billion, which represented a $2.3 billion decrease (improvement) from the prior year, primarily driven by lower noninterest expense and higher revenue. Thus, while both identify 'All Other' as a segment with significant losses or adjustments, C's loss widened due to revenue/tax headwinds, whereas BAC's loss narrowed due to expense and revenue tailwinds.
